verification_standard.$comment: The check that separates 'a backend exists' from 'an operator can reach it'.
verification_standard.why: dist/app.js is go:embed'ed. A frontend source change that was never rebuilt reaches no browser, so a route with no caller in the bundle is a feature nobody can use.
verification_standard.grep_warning: grep here is ugrep and reports zero matches, exiting 0, for any file containing a NUL byte. Use grep -a, or read bytes in python. A positive control on a DIFFERENT symbol does not detect this.

issues.title: Comparer has no diff alignment: one inserted byte reports the whole remainder as changed
issues.description: compareOps walks a[i] against b[i] positionally. There is no LCS/Myers alignment, so any edit that changes length desynchronises every byte after it. The Comparer is a primary tool — an operator compares two responses to decide whether an input changed behaviour — so this makes it near-useless on real traffic, and it can bury a genuine difference in noise rather than merely being ugly.

evidence.command: POST /api/tools/compare with a="the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", b=the same with one char inserted at offset 4
evidence.observed: ops: equal a_len=4, replace a_len=39, insert a_len=0 — 39 of 43 bytes reported changed

scope_notes: The Comparer page already discloses that it compares BYTES rather than words. That is about granularity and is honest; it does not disclose the alignment problem, so an operator reads the output as trustworthy. A fix should reword that notice.
Interacts with 5050ca5 (uninteresting headers), which tags ops by byte offset. The tagging logic survives an alignment change but its test fixtures will need updating.

issues.title: PayloadGenerator's three methods are dead code duplicating the live PayloadSource.Resolve path
issues.description: Intruder payload types genuinely work, via PayloadSource.Resolve (internal/intruder/payload.go:280) called from internal/web/api_tools.go:566. PayloadGenerator now sits beside that as a second, unreachable implementation of the same feature. Two implementations of 'generate numeric payloads' drift, and a fix applied to one will not reach the other.

evidence.command: python3 walk over internal/**/*.go counting non-definition, non-comment references
evidence.observed: GenerateNumbers: 2 refs, both intruder_test.go. GenerateFromFile: 3 refs, all intruder_test.go. GenerateCustom: 0 refs anywhere including tests.
evidence.caution: A raw `grep -c` on these names returns 1 each — the doc comment and the func line. Filter definitions and comments.

issues.suggested_resolution: Delete the three methods, or route PayloadSource.Resolve through them. Either is fine; having both is not.

issues.title: Inverted-range protection is asserted only on a function production never calls
issues.description: That test asserts a fix for an inverted-range panic via GenerateNumbers(5, 1). Production does not call GenerateNumbers (see INTR-DEAD-GEN), so the protection it demonstrates does not apply to the live path. A reader will reasonably conclude otherwise. Whether PayloadSource.Resolve handles an inverted range is currently unasserted either way.
issues.suggested_resolution: Port the assertion to PayloadSource.Resolve, and find out what it actually does with start > end before assuming it is correct.

issues.title: WebSocket interception does not reassemble fragmented messages
issues.description: Burp reassembles fragmented WebSocket messages before offering them for editing. burpsy relays them untouched. A held fragment is half a message, and an edit to it cannot be length-checked against a remainder that has already gone — so refusing is correct until reassembly exists, but it is a real gap.

evidence.observed: FIN-clear and continuation frames return (false, reason) and are relayed

issues.title: WebSocket interception does not inflate compressed (permessage-deflate) frames
issues.description: Any RSV bit set means the payload is a DEFLATE block. Offering it as editable text would be fiction and accepting an edit would put an invalid block on the wire, so it is relayed. Only reachable when the operator has disabled Sec-WebSocket-Extensions stripping, which burpsy does by default — so most connections are unaffected.

evidence.observed: hdr.RSV != 0 returns (false, reason) and is relayed

issues.title: WebSocket match & replace (W6 #55) is not implemented
issues.description: W6 #55 covers both WS interception and WS match/replace. Interception landed in 626ac5f; no WebSocket target exists in the match/replace rule set.

evidence.command: grep for a WebSocket direction/target in internal/matchreplace
evidence.observed: no WS target; matchreplace directions are HTTP request/response only

issues.title: Engine.Forward treats an empty edit as 'unchanged', so a WebSocket payload cannot be cleared
issues.description: Forward(id, edited, fixContentLength) uses the original bytes when edited == "". Harmless for HTTP, where an empty message is meaningless. For a WebSocket frame it means an operator who clears the payload gets the original forwarded instead — the edit silently becomes a no-op.

evidence.observed: if edited != "" { raw = []byte(edited) } — empty falls through to h.Raw

issues.suggested_resolution: Take *string so 'absent' and 'empty' are distinguishable. Touches every caller, which is why it was left rather than changed under the HTTP path.

issues.title: Uninteresting headers are consulted by the Comparer only
issues.description: Burp applies these lists to site-map comparison and scanner response diffing as well. burpsy applies them to the Comparer. The API reports this honestly via applies_to, so no operator is misled about the current reach.

issues.title: LEAD, UNVERIFIED: §9.3c may report Audited where the true state is scoped-not-started
issues.description: Earlier work flagged that AuditItemPoint carries no per-point probe accounting, so an item may be reported Audited when nothing was probed for that point. NOT re-verified at this HEAD. Confirm before filing, then file or discard.

evidence.observed: n/a — this is why state is 'lead'

issues.title: dist/app.js is a tracked whole-tree build artifact, causing multi-agent contention
issues.description: Because it is generated from the whole frontend tree and committed, two agents building concurrently produce a file neither can review hunk by hunk. It cost real coordination time this session. Options: build in CI and stop tracking it, or a documented one-builder protocol.

evidence.observed: touched by separate agents' commits in the same session

issues.title: NUL-byte guard covers frontend sources only
issues.description: TestNoUISourceFileIsInvisibleToGrep walks internal/web/ui/src (86 files). Go's own toolchain rejects NUL in .go input, so the remaining exposure is other tracked text — docs, configs, scripts. Not hypothetical: the bug was re-introduced into a parity document during this session while writing the retraction for it, and caught in the same pass.
issues.suggested_resolution: Extend the walk to all tracked text files, or add a pre-commit check.

cap_gap_rows.counting_warning: Do NOT derive this with awk -F'|' testing field 7. Several notes contain a literal | inside backticked commands (row #80 holds 'MinVersion\|CipherSuites'), which shifts the marker past field 7. Counting that way yields 27/9 instead of 28/8. Join every field after the state column: parts = line.split('|'); state = parts[5].strip().strip('*'); note = '|'.join(parts[6:])
